title: Residential Real Property Transfer Disclosure Statement
description: Alaska Statute §34.70.010 requires the transferor of residential real property (1-4 units) to deliver a written disclosure statement to the prospective transferee. The disclosure covers structural, mechanical, environmental, and material conditions. Failure to disclose known defects may result in liability.

required_actions.note: Disclosure must be provided before transfer. Buyer may rescind within 3 days of receipt if provided late.

title: Agency Relationship Disclosure and Designated Licensee Requirements
description: Alaska Statute §08.88.396 requires written agency disclosure to all parties. Alaska permits designated licensees (where different licensees within the same brokerage represent buyer and seller separately) but a single licensee may not act as a dual agent representing both parties simultaneously. Written consent is required for all agency relationships.

required_actions.note: Dual agency by a single licensee is prohibited. Designated licensees within same brokerage must have written consent from both parties.

title: Escrow/Title Company Closing State
description: Alaska is an escrow closing state. Closings are conducted through title/escrow companies. Attorney presence is not required by statute. Title insurance is standard.

required_actions.note: Title insurance strongly recommended; lender's title insurance required for financed transactions.

title: Seismic and Earthquake Zone Disclosure
description: Alaska's property disclosure statement under AS §34.70.020 requires sellers to disclose known seismic hazards, including whether the property is in a mapped earthquake fault zone, has sustained earthquake damage, or is in a tsunami inundation zone. Given Alaska's high seismicity, this is a critical disclosure item.

required_actions.note: Seismic hazard items included in the statutory disclosure form. Seller must disclose known earthquake damage and fault zone proximity.

title: Well Water and Septic System Disclosure
description: Alaska's property disclosure (AS §34.70.020) requires disclosure of water source type (well, municipal, other) and wastewater system (septic, community sewer). For properties on well water or septic systems, sellers must disclose known deficiencies. DEC regulations may require septic inspection in certain boroughs.

required_actions.note: Disclose water source and septic status on the statutory form. Well water testing recommended.
